summary: The water checks both the woman and the other man. Rabbi Akiva and Rebbi learn from extra words in the pesukim that she becomes forbidden both to her husband and to the other man.

chunks.en: Just as the water checks her,
chunks.st: Just as the water evaluates her fidelity,

chunks.en: so the water checks him (the other man),
chunks.st: so too, the water evaluates his,
chunks.stMore: i.e., her alleged paramour’s, involvement in the sin,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says "And it shall come," and again "And it shall come."
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And the water that causes the curse shall enter into her” (Numbers 5:24), and it is stated again: “And the water that causes the curse shall enter
chunks.stMore: into her and become bitter” (Numbers 5:27). It is derived from the double mention of the phrase “and…shall enter” that both the woman and her paramour are evaluated by the water. Furthermore, prior to her drinking the water,

chunks.en: Just as she is forbidden to her husband,
chunks.st: just as she is forbidden to her husband,

chunks.en: so she is forbidden to the other man,
chunks.st: so too is she forbidden to her paramour,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says "she became tamei"
chunks.st: because in contrast to the verse stating: “Is defiled [nitma’a]” (Numbers 5:14), a superfluous conjoining prefix vav is added to a later verse, rendering the phrase: “

chunks.en: and "and she became tamei." That is what Rabbi Akiva says.
chunks.st: And is defiled [venitma’a]” (Numbers 5:29). The addition indicates another prohibition, that of the woman to her paramour. This is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua said:

chunks.he: כָּךְ הָיָה דוֹרֵשׁ זְכַרְיָה בֶן הַקַּצָּב.
chunks.en: This is how Zecharyah ben HaKatzav used to explain it.
chunks.st: That was how Zekharya ben HaKatzav would interpret
chunks.stMore: it, i.e., he also derived from the superfluous vav that the woman is forbidden to her paramour.

chunks.en: Rebbi says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says

words.note: Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi, who put together the Mishnah.

chunks.en: The two times it is said in the parashah,
chunks.st: an alternate source: The two times that the defilement of the wife is stated in the passage,

chunks.en: "she became tamei," "she became tamei" —
chunks.st: namely: “And he warns his wife, and she is defiled” (Numbers 5:14), and the later verse: “When a wife, being under her husband, goes astray and is defiled”
chunks.stMore: (Numbers 5:29), indicate that her defilement results in two prohibitions.

chunks.en: one is for the husband, and one is for the other man.
chunks.st: One is that she is forbidden to her husband and one is that she is forbidden to her paramour.

summary: Rabbi Akiva taught from a pasuk that a loaf on the second level of tumah can make another loaf tamei on the third level. Rabbi Yehoshua wished his rebbi, Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai, could have heard it.

chunks.en: On that day Rabbi Akiva explained:
chunks.st: On that same day that Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya was appointed head of the Sanhedrin, Rabbi Akiva interpreted the verse: “

chunks.en: "And every clay kli
chunks.st: And every earthen vessel

chunks.en: that one of them falls into,
chunks.st: into which any of them falls,

chunks.en: everything inside it yitma (will be tamei)."
chunks.st: whatever is in it shall be impure [yitma],
chunks.stMore: and you shall break it” (Leviticus 11:33), as follows:

chunks.en: It does not say "tamei," but "yitma,"
chunks.st: The verse does not state: Is impure [tamei], but rather: “Shall be impure,”

chunks.en: to teach that it makes other things tamei.
chunks.st: in order to indicate that not only does the vessel itself become ritually impure, but it can now render other items ritually impure.

chunks.en: This teaches about a loaf that is a sheini (on the second level),
chunks.st: This teaches with regard to a loaf that has second-
chunks.stMore: degree ritual impurity status due to its being placed inside an earthenware vessel that had first-degree impurity,

words.note: A sheini: tamei on the second level.

chunks.en: that it makes a third one tamei.
chunks.st: that it can render other food with which it comes into contact impure with third-degree impurity status.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said,
chunks.st: After hearing Rabbi Akiva’s statement, Rabbi Yehoshua said:

chunks.en: "Who will take the dust off your eyes,
chunks.st: Who will remove the dirt from your eyes,

chunks.en: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai!
chunks.st: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai, so that you could live and see this?

chunks.en: For you used to say,
chunks.st: As you would say:

chunks.he: עָתִיד דּוֹר אַחֵר לְטַהֵר כִּכָּר שְׁלִישִׁי,
chunks.en: 'Some day, another generation will say a third-level loaf is tahor,
chunks.st: In the future, another generation is destined to deem pure a loaf that contracted third-degree impurity,

chunks.he: שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מִקְרָא מִן הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא.
chunks.en: because there is no pasuk in the Torah that says it is tamei.'
chunks.st: as there is no explicit verse from the Torah stating that it is impure.

chunks.en: But here is Akiva, your student, bringing
chunks.st: But now Rabbi Akiva, your disciple, brings

chunks.en: a pasuk from the Torah that it is tamei,
chunks.st: a verse from the Torah indicating that it is impure,

chunks.en: as it says, 'Whatever is inside it yitma.'"
chunks.st: as it is stated: “Whatever is in it shall be impure.”

summary: Two pesukim give different sizes for the land around the cities of the Leviim. Rabbi Akiva explains that the extra two thousand amos teach the techum of Shabbos, and Rabbi Eliezer says they are fields and vineyards.

chunks.en: On that day Rabbi Akiva explained:
chunks.st: on that same day Rabbi Akiva interpreted the verses with regard to the Levite cities as follows: One verse states: “

chunks.en: "And you shall measure outside the city
chunks.st: And you shall measure outside the city

chunks.he: אֶת פְּאַת קֵדְמָה אַלְפַּיִם בָּאַמָּה וְגוֹ',
chunks.en: on the east side two thousand amos," and so on.
chunks.st: for the east side two thousand cubits…
chunks.stMore: this shall be for them the open land outside the cities” (Numbers 35:5),

chunks.en: And another pasuk says,
chunks.st: and another verse states:
chunks.stMore: “And the open land around the cities, which you shall give to the Levites, shall be

chunks.he: מִקִּיר הָעִיר וָחוּצָה אֶלֶף אַמָּה סָבִיב.
chunks.en: "from the wall of the city outward, a thousand amos all around."
chunks.st: from the wall of the city and outward one thousand cubits round about” (Numbers 35:4).

chunks.en: We cannot say a thousand amos,
chunks.st: It is impossible to say that the area around the cities given to the Levites was only one thousand cubits,

chunks.en: since it already says two thousand amos.
chunks.st: as it is already stated: “Two thousand cubits.”

chunks.en: And we cannot say two thousand amos,
chunks.st: And it is impossible to say that two thousand cubits were left for them,

chunks.en: since it already says a thousand amos.
chunks.st: as it is already stated: “One thousand cubits.”

chunks.en: So how does it work?
chunks.st: How can these texts be reconciled?

chunks.en: A thousand amos are open land around the city,
chunks.st: One thousand cubits are to be set aside as a tract of open land surrounding the city,

words.note: Open land around a city of the Leviim.

chunks.en: and two thousand amos are the techum of Shabbos.
chunks.st: and the two thousand cubits are mentioned not in order to be given to the Levites, but to indicate the boundary of the Shabbat limit,
chunks.stMore: beyond which it is forbidden to travel on Shabbat. This verse thereby serves as the source for the two-thousand-cubit Shabbat limit.

words.note: Techum: how far one may walk outside a city on Shabbos.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer, the son of
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer, son of

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, says otherwise:

chunks.en: A thousand amos are open land,
chunks.st: One thousand cubits were given to the Levites as an open tract
chunks.stMore: of land, that could not be planted or built upon,

chunks.en: and two thousand amos are for fields and vineyards.
chunks.st: and two thousand cubits of additional land were given to the Levites for planting fields and vineyards.

summary: Rabbi Akiva learns from the word "saying" that at the Yam Suf, Klal Yisrael answered after Moshe on every line of the Shirah, like Hallel. Rabbi Nechemyah says they sang it together, like Shema.

chunks.he: בּוֹ בַיּוֹם דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא (שמות טו),
chunks.en: On that day Rabbi Akiva explained:
chunks.st: on that same day Rabbi Akiva interpreted the verse:

chunks.en: "Then Moshe and Bnei Yisrael sang
chunks.st: “Then Moses and the children of Israel sang

chunks.en: this song to Hashem,
chunks.st: this song to the Lord,

chunks.en: and they said, saying."
chunks.st: and said, saying” (Exodus 15:1), as follows:

chunks.en: There was no need to say "saying,"
chunks.st: As there is no need for the verse to state the word “saying,”
chunks.stMore: because it states the word “said” immediately prior to it,

chunks.en: so why does it say "saying"?
chunks.st: why must the verse state the word “saying”?

chunks.he: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹנִין אַחֲרָיו שֶׁל משֶׁה
chunks.en: It teaches that Klal Yisrael answered after Moshe
chunks.st: It teaches that the Jewish people would repeat in song after Moses

chunks.en: on every single line,
chunks.st: every single statement he said,

chunks.en: like when we say Hallel.
chunks.st: as is done when reciting hallel. After Moses would recite a verse, they would say as a refrain: “I will sing to the Lord, for He is highly exalted” (Exodus 15:1). It is

chunks.en: That is why it says "saying."
chunks.st: for this reason that the word “saying” is stated, in addition to the word “said.”

chunks.en: Rabbi Nechemyah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Neḥemya says: The people sang the song together with Moses

chunks.en: Like when we say Shema,
chunks.st: as is done when reciting Shema,
chunks.stMore: which is recited in unison after the prayer leader begins,

chunks.en: and not like when we say Hallel.
chunks.st: and not as is done when reciting hallel.

summary: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Hurkanos taught from the pesukim that Iyov served Hashem out of love, not only out of fear. Rabbi Yehoshua wished Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai could have heard it.

chunks.he: בּוֹ בַיּוֹם דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן הוּרְקְנוֹס,
chunks.en: On that day Rabbi Yehoshua ben Hurkanos explained:
chunks.st: On that same day Rabbi Yehoshua ben Hyrcanus taught:

chunks.he: לֹא עָבַד אִיּוֹב אֶת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
chunks.en: Iyov did not serve Hakadosh Baruch Hu
chunks.st: Job served the Holy One, Blessed be He,

chunks.en: except out of love,
chunks.st: only out of love,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "Even if He kills me, I will hope to Him."
chunks.st: “Though He will slay me, still I will trust in Him” (Job 13:15).

chunks.en: But the matter is still unclear:
chunks.st: And still, the matter is even,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the verse is ambiguous, as there are two possible interpretations of the verse.

chunks.he: לוֹ אֲנִי מְצַפֶּה אוֹ אֵינִי מְצַפֶּה,
chunks.en: does it mean "I wait for Him," or "I do not wait"?
chunks.st: Was Job saying: I will await Him, expressing his yearning for God; or should the verse be interpreted as saying I will not await
chunks.stMore: Him. As the word “lo” can mean either “to him” or “not,” it is unclear which meaning is intended here.

chunks.en: So the pasuk teaches:
chunks.st: This dilemma is resolved elsewhere, where the verse states a clearer indication of Job’s intent:

chunks.he: עַד אֶגְוָע לֹא אָסִיר תֻּמָּתִי מִמֶּנִּי,
chunks.en: "Until I die, I will not give up my innocence."
chunks.st: “Till I die I will not put away my integrity from me” (Job 27:5).

chunks.en: This teaches that he did it out of love.
chunks.st: This teaches that he acted out of love.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua said:

chunks.en: "Who will take the dust off your eyes,
chunks.st: Who will remove the dirt from your eyes,

chunks.en: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai!
chunks.st: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai, so that you could live and see this?

chunks.en: All your life you explained
chunks.st: As you taught all your life

chunks.he: שֶׁלֹּא עָבַד אִיּוֹב אֶת הַמָּקוֹם אֶלָּא מִיִּרְאָה,
chunks.en: that Iyov served Hashem only out of fear,
chunks.st: that Job worshipped the Omnipresent only out of fear,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says,
chunks.st: as it is stated: “

chunks.he: אִישׁ תָּם וְיָשָׁר יְרֵא אֱלֹהִים וְסָר מֵרָע,
chunks.en: 'a man who was whole and straight, who feared Hashem and stayed away from bad.'
chunks.st: And that man was wholehearted and upright, and God-fearing, and shunned evil” (Job 1:1);

chunks.en: But now Yehoshua, the student of your student,
chunks.st: but now Yehoshua ben Hyrcanus, the disciple of your disciple,

chunks.en: taught that he did it out of love!"
chunks.st: has taught that Job acted out of love.
